recursive.description: Take every image in folders given as inputs, at any depth.

in_place.description: Allow outputs to replace their inputs.

preview.description: Also return the first file written as a picture, fit to 1024 pixels.

tools.name: run
tools.title: egami run
tools.description: Run steps over images, separated by +: 'egami run in.jpg auto-orient + resize 1200x + sharpen 0.6 + save out.webp --quality 82'. Every Egami operation is a step ('egami run --list'); save writes, and may come more than once.

inputs.description: Image files, globs (*, ?, **) or folders with recursive.

workflow.description: The steps of 'egami run' as a file: one object per step, with the step's options as properties. 'egami run --list' lists the steps and their options.

list_steps.description: List every step with its options, instead of running anything.

output.description: Where a save without a path writes, and where the plan writes when it has no save: a file, folder, template or -.

save_workflow.description: Write the steps to a JSON workflow file (then run them, unless --dry-run).

dry_run.description: Print the steps and the files each input would write, and stop.

to.description: Convert colors to this profile while reading.

recursive.description: Take every image in folders given as inputs.

in_place.description: Allow outputs to replace their inputs.

preview.description: Also return the first file written as a picture, fit to 1024 pixels.

value.description: An option's value: text as the command line writes it (a size, a color, x,y), a number or true or false.

op.description: The step's name, such as resize, blur or save.

path.description: Where to write; without it the save writes to -o. Templates such as out/{name}.webp work.

format.description: The format by name or extension, when the path's extension does not say.

set.description: Writer settings as in --set: keys such as png.compression-level, values as text, numbers or true or false.

tools.name: compare
tools.title: egami compare
tools.description: Compare two images: print a metric and exit with 1 when they differ more than --threshold.

other.description: The image to compare it with, the same size.

metric.description: The number to print and test: ae (pixels that differ), mae, mse, rmse (the default), peak, psnr, ssim or dssim.

threshold.description: Exit with 1 when the metric is worse than this (above it, or below it for psnr and ssim); without it, any difference exits with 1.

fuzz.description: How far apart two values may be and still count as equal, from 0 to 1, for ae and the exit code.

diff.description: Write a picture of the differences.

diff_style.description: highlight (differing pixels in red, as ImageMagick's compare) or absolute (|a - b|).

preview.description: Also return the first file written as a picture, fit to 1024 pixels.

tools.description: Measure images: per-channel minimum, maximum, mean, deviation, skewness, kurtosis and entropy, as ImageMagick's identify -verbose.

input.description: The animation, or - for standard input.

output.description: A template for each frame's file: {frame} or {index} is the frame number from 0, padded as in {frame:000}; {name} is the input's name.

format.description: The output format, when the template's extension does not say.

delays.description: Also write each frame's delay in milliseconds, one per line, to this file, so 'frames join --delays' can restore the timing.

preview.description: Also return the first file written as a picture, fit to 1024 pixels.

delays.description: A file of delays in milliseconds, one per frame, as 'frames split --delays' writes.

loop.description: How many times the animation plays; 0 (the default) loops forever.

preview.description: Also return the first file written as a picture, fit to 1024 pixels.
